title: {Syn} RSA Turns Factoring Into a Lock
content:
RSA public-key cryptography relies on arithmetic modulo a product of two large primes. Multiplication is easy, but recovering the primes from their product is believed to be hard at the sizes used in practice.

The design is a clean example of a one-way trapdoor: anyone can use the public key to encrypt or verify, while the private key uses hidden factorization information.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
